title: J063 Service and Software Updates to Security Access Control and Camera Systems Across Idaho/ Eastern Oregon VA Locations
description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. This is not a solicitation for bids, proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The purpose of this Sources Sought Notice is to obtain information regarding the availability and capability of all qualified sources to perform a potential requirement. The responses received from interested contractors will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method. The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Network Contracting Office (NCO) 20, is conducting market research to identify potential sources which can provide the following services: Title: Service and Software Updates to Security Access Control and Camera Systems NAICS Code: 561621, Security Systems Services (except Locksmiths) Locations: varies across Idaho/ Eastern Oregon VA, see below Tasks: Overview: the Contractor shall monitor the CBOCs in Caldwell, Twin Falls, Mountain Home, and Boise VAMC Logistics Warehouse internal or external doors and motion alarms. This requirement include alarm monitoring and possible service calls to all locations, including the Boise VA Medical Center (see below). The contract will also include security cameras, PIV card readers, and software updates from the Contractor. Software updates improve performance, add features, and patch vulnerabilities, keeping systems secure and compliant. Contractor shall respond to calls for service to maintain, repair, and/or replace needed hardware and/or software to correct problems associated with the following: any/all burglar alarm systems, video operations components and systems, Lenel Alarm Monitoring system, Milestone CCTV Software and hardware, and the Roam Alert Patient Management System. If Contractor replaces a non-operational burglar alarm system, the Contractor shall assume monitoring of the new system immediately. Contractor shall be requested by an authorized employee of the BVAMC to inspect, repair, or replace all systems related to burglar alarm systems, Lenel Security system, Milestone video management system, and associated parts or systems controlled by these systems to include; card readers, cameras, software updates, motion sensors, door/window contacts, dialers, switches, wires, conduit, circuit boards, wired or wireless communication systems, and other miscellaneous parts or accessories needed to repair or replace broken parts or systems. In addition to repairing the current video and access control systems, the Contractor shall, at the request of authorized employee of BVAMC, install new hardware or software to expand the abilities of the video or access control systems. Contractor may be asked to provide parts to the Boise VA when VA employees will complete the installation of those parts. The Contractor can be asked to provide spare items that the VA needs to have in stock. The Contractor shall respond to emergency service calls to the following locations and timeframes: Boise VA Medical Center, 500 W. Fort Street, Boise, Idaho 83702 (2-hour response time) Caldwell CBOC, 713 Haystack Wy, Caldwell, ID 83605 (2-hour response time) Eastern Oregon CBOC, 635 Hwy 20 N Suite #4, Hines, OR 97738 (6-hour response time) Mountain Home CBOC, 815 North 6th East, Mountain Home, ID 83647 (3-hour response time) Salmon CBOC, 705 Lena Street, Salmon, ID 83467 (8-hour response time) Twin Falls CBOC, 260 2nd Ave East, Twin Falls, ID 83301 (4-hour response time) Twin Falls Annex, 450 Falls Ave, Suite 108, Twin Falls, ID 83301 (4-hour response time) Vet Center, 2424 Bank Drive, Boise, ID 83702 (2-hour response time) River Street Clinic, 1276 River Street #203, Boise, ID 83702 (2-hour response time) Veterans Cemetery, 1585 East Elm St (E 4150 N), Buhl, Idaho 83316 (4-hour response time) Contractor shall electronically send the available updates to the VA Police Physical Security Officer, or come to the VA and install them from portable media. Due to the importance of this service, VA requests a minimum of a 2-hour response time. Additional Market Research and Considerations: The current requirement involves existing LenelS2 OnGuard and Milestone Systems software and hardware. The VA is reviewing if brand name or equal entities can participate that offer a solution compatible with existing LenelS2 OnGuard and Milestone Systems software and hardware, as well as authorized to work on existing equipment. Current requirements state Contractor shall employ local individuals with the following minimum certifications: Milestone Certified Integration Engineer (MCIE) and LenelS2 OnGuard Certified Expert. The requirement also requires as needed expansions and repair of existing Level, Milestone and Roam Alert video and access control systems. Period of Performance: Estimate 2/1/2026 � 1/31/2027, plus Option Years 1-4. Potential candidates having the capabilities necessary to provide the above stated services are invited to respond to this Sources Sought Notice via e-mail to Danielle Carrico at Danielle.Carrico@va.gov no later than 10/28/2026 at 5PM PT. title: Z--NOTICE OF JUSTIFICATION AND APPROVAL
description: The Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command, Europe Africa Central (NAVFAC EURAFCENT) intends to extend the ordering period for the Mini Multiple Award Construction Contract (Mini MACC) for an additional 12 months, from September 2, 2026, to September 1, 2027. This is a bridge action and does not increase the original $95 million contract ceiling. The extension will utilize the remaining contract capacity of approximately $44 million. Incumbent Contractors: Liberal Construction, LLC Consorzio Continental Socconsortile A R RocKs GMBH Kooheji Contractors Macro Vantage Levant DMCC Justification: The extension is required due to "unusual and compelling urgency" under the authority of 10 U.S.C. � 3204(a)(2). Critical Mission Impact: A lapse in construction services at NSA Bahrain, the forward headquarters of the U.S. Fifth Fleet, would result in an unacceptable inability to perform emergency repairs and would degrade U.S. national security during a period of heightened operational activity in the region. Procurement Delays: The procurement of a long-term, competitive follow-on contract has been severely impacted by unforeseen events and the reassignment of key personnel to support critical operational priorities ("Operation Epic Fury"). Impracticality of Alternatives: Awarding a new contract vehicle at this time would cause an unavoidable and mission-critical delay of several months due to security, legal, and logistical requirements in Bahrain. This bridge action is necessary to provide the time required to complete the full and open competition for the follow-on MACC without incurring a dangerous gap in critical construction services.

description: White City, Oregon, Boiler Inspection Services Solicitation Base Year + Four Option Years The objective of this solicitation is to provide VA Southern Oregon Rehabilitation Center and Clinics (VA SORCC) with Boiler Plant Inspection Services. The resulting contract should be for one base year and four options years as follows: Base Year: 11/1/2026 to 10/31/2027. Option Year 1: 11/1/2027 to 10/31/2028 Option Year 2: 11/1/2028 to 10/31/2029 Option Year 3: 11/1/2029 to 10/31/2030 Option Year 4: 11/1/2030 to 10/31/2031 Details: The VA SORCC has three heating boilers, each rated at 250HP operating at low pressure (<15 psi), gas and oiled fired. Yearly state inspections are required on all three boilers, one deaerator/ feed water tank, one heat recovery tank, one condensate tank, and one bottom blow tank. (3) Three heating boilers, each rated at 250HP (operating pressure <15psi), gas and oil fired. (1) One heat recovery tank (Option Year 1 and 3 only) (1) One condensate tank (Option Year 1 and 3 only) (1) One bottom blow tank (Option Year 1 and 3 only) Inspections to include a TYPE �A� Internal and External inspection and a TYPE �C� External inspection under steam pressure for each boiler. The contractor shall witness and sign a checklist of boiler safety devises as per VA-SORCC testing procedures during the external operational inspection and shall provide a written inspection report upon completion of each inspection to Facilities Management Service. The checklist of required safety devises to be tested will be available to the contractor The inspections are to be scheduled anytime throughout the term of the contract at the discretion of the Boiler Plant Lead. Why an Inspector Must Be Present Legal Compliance: Without an inspector�s presence and approval, the NDT cannot be considered valid for regulatory purposes. title: J063 Service and Software Updates to Security Access Control and Camera Systems Across Idaho/ Eastern Oregon VA Locations
description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. This is not a solicitation for bids, proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The purpose of this Sources Sought Notice is to obtain information regarding the availability and capability of all qualified sources to perform a potential requirement. The responses received from interested contractors will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method. The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Network Contracting Office (NCO) 20, is conducting market research to identify potential sources which can provide the following services: Title: Service and Software Updates to Security Access Control and Camera Systems NAICS Code: 561621, Security Systems Services (except Locksmiths) Locations: varies across Idaho/ Eastern Oregon VA, see below Tasks: Overview: the Contractor shall monitor the CBOCs in Caldwell, Twin Falls, Mountain Home, and Boise VAMC Logistics Warehouse internal or external doors and motion alarms. This requirement include alarm monitoring and possible service calls to all locations, including the Boise VA Medical Center (see below). The contract will also include security cameras, PIV card readers, and software updates from the Contractor. Software updates improve performance, add features, and patch vulnerabilities, keeping systems secure and compliant. Contractor shall respond to calls for service to maintain, repair, and/or replace needed hardware and/or software to correct problems associated with the following: any/all burglar alarm systems, video operations components and systems, Lenel Alarm Monitoring system, Milestone CCTV Software and hardware, and the Roam Alert Patient Management System. If Contractor replaces a non-operational burglar alarm system, the Contractor shall assume monitoring of the new system immediately. Contractor shall be requested by an authorized employee of the BVAMC to inspect, repair, or replace all systems related to burglar alarm systems, Lenel Security system, Milestone video management system, and associated parts or systems controlled by these systems to include; card readers, cameras, software updates, motion sensors, door/window contacts, dialers, switches, wires, conduit, circuit boards, wired or wireless communication systems, and other miscellaneous parts or accessories needed to repair or replace broken parts or systems. In addition to repairing the current video and access control systems, the Contractor shall, at the request of authorized employee of BVAMC, install new hardware or software to expand the abilities of the video or access control systems. Contractor may be asked to provide parts to the Boise VA when VA employees will complete the installation of those parts. The Contractor can be asked to provide spare items that the VA needs to have in stock. The Contractor shall respond to emergency service calls to the following locations and timeframes: Boise VA Medical Center, 500 W. The VA is reviewing if brand name or equal entities can participate that offer a solution compatible with existing LenelS2 OnGuard and Milestone Systems software and hardware, as well as authorized to work on existing equipment.
